A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same probabilistic neural-network verification work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and support comparison, including the rotated results tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original verification experiments on FairSquare, ACAS Xu and MiniACSIncome, plus an appendix comparison of branch-selection heuristics.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on the retained benchmarks and adds controlled comparisons of splitting heuristics and bound-propagation procedures.

M1.justification: v2 extends bounded-input splitting to unbounded continuous and integer inputs, introduces BaBSB-LongestEdge-k, and adds adaptations for multivariate Gaussian distributions and polytopal domains. It removes SelectProbLogBounds and generalizes PV's outer interval-arithmetic call to ComputeBounds. These are substantive procedural extensions, although the central probability-bounding framework remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FairSquare demographic parity and parity of qualified persons, including clipped distributions; ACAS Xu safety and robustness; and MiniACSIncome. The fuller fairness comparison already exists in v1's appendix. The Gaussian and polytope extensions do not introduce evaluated datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets remain FairSquare, SpaceScanner, ProVe_SLR, ε-ProVe and enumeration in their respective benchmarks. Internal comparison methods change: the SelectProb versus SelectProbLogBounds study is replaced by comparisons involving LongestEdge, BaBSB, BaBSB-LongestEdge-10, interval arithmetic and CROWN.

E3.justification: The main experiments switch from SelectProbLogBounds to SelectProb. FairSquare uses unbounded inputs instead of v1's finite limits chosen at machine precision. The replacement appendix studies use FairSquare on HW1, whereas v1's selection study used several benchmarks on HW2. Main metrics, time budgets and MiniACSIncome training splits remain.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix D compares branch-selection heuristics. v2 Appendix E replaces this with controlled tests of splitting heuristics and interval arithmetic versus CROWN, directly examining the performance cost of the completeness-compatible hybrid. Appendix D.2 also adds investigation of the remaining clipped-distribution timeout, including alternative splitting heuristics.

E5.justification: Both retain five training restarts for MiniACSIncome, fixed-seed tie breaking for BaBSB, and ε-ProVe's 99.9% confidence reporting. Neither adds repeated-verification run counts, confidence intervals for runtime, or significance tests. PV's deterministic probability bounds remain distinct from statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Under revised settings, v1 Table 4's NN3,2/Bayes Net 1 qualified-persons timeout becomes a fair result in 40 seconds in v2 Table 3. NN2,2/Bayes Net 1 changes from 622.2 to 11 seconds, reversing its ordering against FairSquare's approximately 60 seconds. ACAS Xu and MiniACSIncome values also change, and new ablations report substantial differences in solved instances. These are revised-configuration results, not isolated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v1's completeness argument concerns SelectProb, interval arithmetic and LongestEdge. v2 introduces explicit convergence and alternation definitions, generalizes the completeness theorem, and develops proofs covering unbounded inputs and the hybrid heuristic. New Appendix C supplies a CROWN non-isotonicity counterexample and a convergence argument using the CROWN Interval Extension.

C1.justification: The abstract and four principal contributions retain their meaning. The introduction revises its quantitative speed claim for FairSquare timeout cases from under ten seconds to under one minute, and updates the ACAS Xu mean runtime from 18 to 21 seconds. The overall claims of faster probabilistic verification and conditional completeness remain.

C2.justification: v1 discusses a non-clipped fairness timeout as potentially reflecting proximity to the fairness threshold. v2 instead investigates the remaining clipped-distribution timeout and suggests an intricate decision boundary in a region of substantial probability mass. It also explicitly distinguishes empirically effective BaBSB from the completeness-compatible hybrid. Existing sampling and population-model limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix C documents CROWN's bounding rules, layer-bound construction and the distinction from CROWN-IBP, where v1 mainly names the employed routine. The HW2 description disappears with its experiment. The code and benchmark access information, main hardware, training hyperparameters and deterministic tie-breaking details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated discussion and multiple references on Bayesian neural-network verification, explaining its different source and dimensionality of uncertainty. It substantially develops the comparison with FairSquare and ProVe_SLR, especially exact probability computation versus iterative bounds, and updates verification and learned-branching references. These changes extend research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The seven-section main narrative remains recognizable. Related work is subdivided and reordered, the interval-arithmetic primer is condensed, and terminology and explanatory prose are edited throughout. The new input-distribution section and theoretical appendix expand the structure, while much of the benchmark and training documentation is retained.

P2.justification: The main FairSquare table is replaced by a cumulative-runtime plot using the fuller appendix comparison. The old selection-heuristic plot is removed, two ablation plots and CROWN pseudocode displays are added, and the interval-arithmetic pseudocode display disappears. Most existing figures and table designs remain, with relocation and modest layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v1's completeness argument covered interval arithmetic with LongestEdge, while its effective experiments used CROWN and BaBSB. v2 substantially strengthens the connection between theory and practice through the CROWN convergence analysis, a completeness-compatible hybrid, and experiments showing that hybrid solves all 18 FairSquare instances. Explicit unbounded-input handling also removes v1's truncation workaround. These gains outweigh the loss of the broader branch-selection study.
